Preface
The intent of the System Impact Study is to determine a plan, with approximate cost and
construction time estimates, to connect the subject generation interconnection project to the PJM
network at a location specified by the Interconnection Customer. As a requirement for
interconnection, the Interconnection Customer may be responsible for the cost of constructing:
Network Upgrades, which are facility additions, or upgrades to existing facilities, that are needed
to maintain the reliability of the PJM system. All facilities required for interconnection of a
generation interconnection project must be designed to meet the technical specifications (on PJM
web site) for the appropriate transmission owner.
In some instances an Interconnection Customer may not be responsible for 100% of the
identified network upgrade cost because other transmission network uses, e.g. another generation
interconnection or merchant transmission upgrade, may also contribute to the need for the same
network reinforcement. The possibility of sharing the reinforcement costs with other projects
may be identified in the Feasibility Study, but the actual allocation will be deferred until the
System Impact Study is performed.
The System Impact Study estimates do not include the feasibility, cost, or time required to obtain
property rights and permits for construction of the required facilities. The project developer is
responsible for the right of way, real estate, and construction permit issues. For properties
currently owned by Transmission Owners, the costs may be included in the study.
General
Tenaska Pennsylvania Partners LLC (“Interconnection Customer”) has proposed an incremental
increase (uprate) to prior queue requests T174 and AB1-106 consisting of natural gas, 2x1
combined cycle generating facility in Westmoreland County, PA. The increased capability
associated with queue position AC1-106 is achieved through planned efficiencies that maximize
the utilization of existing plant equipment to increase its output. The following table shows the
values representing the incremental MFO MW for each unit:

The installed facilities will have a total capability of 1050 MW (MFO) with 940 MW of this
output being recognized by PJM as Capacity Interconnection Rights (CIR). The proposed in-
service date for this project is January 1, 2019. This study does not imply a West Penn Power
Company (“Transmission Owner”) commitment to this in-service date.
Point of Interconnection
AC1-021 project will deliver power to the West Penn transmission system using the same Point
of Interconnection (POI) of prior queue requests T174 and AB1-106. This POI is inside the

Rhodes Lane substation as shown in the one-line diagram in Appendix 2. Rhodes Lane
substation is a three breaker ring bus station that is located approximately 2.8 miles away from
Yukon substation and approximately 29.6 miles from Hatfield substation. The combined cycle
generation site is located approximately 1.5 miles from Rhodes Lane switching station.
Cost Summary
There are no costs associated with the AC1-021 project.
Please Note: All network upgrades and costs associated with the Yukon-Hatfield 500 kV project
are shown in the Facilities Study Reports of prior queue requests (T174 and AB1-106) which are
published on PJM website at http://www.pjm.com/pub/planning/project-
queues/facilities/t174_fac.pdf for T174 and at http://www.pjm.com/pub/planning/project-
queues/facilities/ab1106_fac.pdf for AB1-106.

Executive Summary
Generator Interconnection Request AC1-021 is for an increase in energy injection
capability of the 2x1 combined cycle facility interconnection request AB1-106. The uprate
increases the Maximum Facility Output (MFO) of the plant from 940 MW to 1050 MW.
AC1-021 has a Point of Interconnection (POI) at a tap on the Hatfield – Yukon 500 kV
line in the Allegheny Power System (APS), Fayette County, Pennsylvania.
This report describes a dynamic simulation analysis of AC1-021 as part of the overall
system impact study.
The load flow scenario for the analysis was based on the RTEP 2020 light load case,
modified to include applicable queue projects. AC1-021 has been dispatched online at
maximum power output, with leading power factor and less than 1.0 pu voltage at the
generator bus.
Simulated NERC Standard TPL-001 faults include:
1. Three-phase (3ph) fault with normal clearing (Category P1)
2. Operating of a line section w/o a fault, Single-line-to-ground (slg) on Bus Section
and Breaker. (Category P2)
3. Single-line-to-ground (slg) with delayed clearing as a result of breaker failure
(Category P4)
4. Single-line-to-ground (slg) with delayed clearing as a result of protection failure
(Category P5)
5. Single-line-to-ground (slg) with normal clearing for common structure (Category
P7)
Note: For generator interconnection studies, Category P3 and P6 faults will be studied
on an as needed basis. In this study, P2 contingencies are covered by P1 and P4
contingencies.
The system was tested for a system intact condition and the fault types listed above.
Specific fault descriptions and breaker clearing times used for this study are provided in
the result table.
No relevant High Speed Reclosing (HSR) contingencies were identified.
Maintenance outages (P6) contingencies are also tested in this study.
For all simulations, the queue project under study along with the rest of the PJM system
were required to maintain synchronism and with all states returning to an acceptable
new condition following the disturbance.
The stability criteria was not met for any of the four maintenance outage contingencies
(with a single Ronco unit offline as per the current operational mitigation for these
outages) tested on the RTEP 2020 light load case, with results showing,
 AC1-021 units, AA2-173/AB1-106 units and Ronco Units unstable for the P6
contingency MB.P1.18.
 AC1-021 units, AA2-173/AB1-106 units and Ronco Units unstable for the
contingency MB.P4.10.

 AC1-021 units, AA2-173/AB1-106 units and Ronco Units unstable for the
contingency MB.P4.11.
New operational mitigation for these outages has been proposed which is to reduce
AC1-021 generation dispatch by 110 MW and open Ft.Martin-FL-8 breaker.
For the remaining contingencies tested on the 2020 light load case:
a) The system with AC1-021 included is transiently stable and post-contingency
oscillations were positively damped with a damping margin of at least 3%.
b) The AC1-021 generators were able to ride through faults (except for faults where
protective action trips AC1-021).
c) Following fault clearing, all bus voltages recover to a minimum of 0.7 per unit
after 2.5 seconds (except where protective action isolates that bus).
d) No transmission element trips, other than those either directly connected or
designed to trip as a consequence of that fault.
No mitigations were found to be required.

1. Introduction
Generator Interconnection Request AC1-021 is for an increase in energy injection
capability of the 2x1 combined cycle facility interconnection request AB1-106. The uprate
increases the Maximum Facility Output (MFO) of the plant from 940 MW to 1050 MW.
AC1-021 has a Point of Interconnection (POI) at a tap on the Hatfield – Yukon 500 kV
line in the Allegheny Power System (APS), Fayette County, Pennsylvania.
This analysis is effectively a screening study to determine whether the addition of AC1-
021 will meet the dynamic requirements of the NERC, PJM and Transmission Owner
reliability standards.
In this report the AC1-021 project and how it is proposed to be connected to the grid are
first described, followed by a description of how the project is modeled in this study. The
fault cases are then described and analyzed, and lastly a discussion of the results is
provided.

3. Loadflow and Dynamics Case Setup
The dynamics simulation analysis was carried out using PSS/E Version 33.7.
The load flow scenario and fault cases for this study are based on PJM’s Regional
Transmission Planning Process1.
The selected load flow scenario is the RTEP 2020 light load case with the following
modifications:
a) Addition of all applicable queue projects prior to AC1-021.
b) Addition of AC1-021 queue project.
c) Removal of withdrawn and subsequent queue projects in the vicinity of AC1-021.
d) Dispatch of units in the PJM system to maintain slack generators within limits.
The AC1-021 initial conditions are listed in Table , indicating maximum power output,
with unity power factor at the generator bus.

4. Fault Cases
Tables 3 to 10 list the contingencies that were studied, with representative worst case
total clearing times provided by PJM. Each contingency was studied over a 10 second
simulation time interval.
The studied contingencies include:
a) Steady state operation (Category P0);
b) Three-phase (3ph) fault with normal clearing (Category P1)
c) Single-line-to-ground (slg) with delayed clearing as a result of breaker failure
(Category P4)
d) Single-line-to-ground (slg) with delayed clearing as a result of protection failure
(Category P5)
e) Three phase faults with normal clearing time with maintenance outages of Fort
Martin – Ronco 500 kV line;
f) Three phase faults with normal clearing time with maintenance outages of AC1-
021 – Yukon 500 kV line;
g) Single phase faults with stuck breaker with maintenance outages of AC1-021 –
Yukon 500 kV line; and
h) Three phase faults with stuck breaker with maintenance outages of AC1-021 –
Yukon 500 kV line.
No relevant Bus, Tower or High Speed Reclosing (HSR) contingencies were identified.
Clearing times listed in Tables 3 to 10 are as per Revision 18 of “2016 Revised Clearing
times for each PJM company” spreadsheet.
Attachment 2 contains the one-line diagrams of the APS network in the vicinity of AC1-
021, showing where faults were applied.
The positive sequence fault impedances for single line to ground faults were derived
from a separate short circuit case, modified to ensure that connected generators in the
vicinity of AC1-021 have not withdrawn from the PJM queue, and are not greater than
the queue position under study.

5. Evaluation Criteria
This study is focused on AC1-021, along with the rest of the PJM system, maintaining
synchronism and having all states return to an acceptable new condition following the
disturbance. The recovery criteria applicable to this study are as per PJM’s Regional
Transmission Planning Process and Transmission Owner criteria:
a) The system with AC1-021 included is transiently stable and post-contingency
oscillations should be positively damped with a damping margin of at least 3%.
b) The AC1-021 is able to ride through faults (except for faults where protective
action trips AC1-021).
c) Following fault clearing, all bus voltages recover to a minimum of 0.7 per unit
after 2.5 seconds (except where protective action isolates that bus).
d) No transmission element trips, other than those either directly connected or
designed to trip as a consequence of that fault.
